chapters.title: The Sun and the Solar System’s Edge

levels.title: Your Cosmic Address
levels.objective: After this level you can state Earth's address: third planet from the Sun, a star in the Milky Way.

levels.title: The Sun, Up Close
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what powers the Sun and how dominant it is in the solar system.

levels.title: The Rocky Four
levels.objective: After this level you can name the rocky planets and explain why Venus, not Mercury, is the hottest.

levels.title: Giants of the Outer Dark
levels.objective: After this level you can tell gas giants from ice giants and describe Jupiter's and Saturn's standout features.

levels.title: Why We Have Seasons
levels.objective: After this level you can explain that seasons come from Earth's tilt, not its distance from the Sun.

levels.title: The Moon's Changing Face
levels.objective: After this level you can explain Moon phases and why we only ever see one side of the Moon.

levels.title: Eclipses and a Cosmic Coincidence
levels.objective: After this level you can tell solar from lunar eclipses and explain why the Moon can exactly cover the Sun.

levels.title: Light-Years: Measuring the Unmeasurable
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what a light-year measures and how far the nearest star is.

levels.title: The Life of a Star
levels.objective: After this level you can read a star's temperature from its color and outline how the Sun will end.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Your Place in the Universe
levels.objective: After this level you can trace Earth's address from our planet all the way out to the observable universe.

levels.title: Why the Sky Turns
levels.objective: After this level you can explain that day and night, and the stars rising and setting, come from Earth spinning.

levels.title: A Year Around the Sun
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what a year is, why leap years exist, and why the night sky changes with the seasons.

levels.title: Connect the Dots: Constellations
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what a constellation is and why its stars usually aren’t near each other.

levels.title: The North Star
levels.objective: After this level you can find north with Polaris and explain why some stars never set.

levels.title: The Ecliptic: The Planets’ Highway
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why the Sun, Moon and planets all travel along the same narrow band of sky.

levels.title: Wanderers: How Planets Move Across the Sky
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why planets drift against the stars and sometimes appear to loop backwards.

levels.title: Tides: The Moon’s Pull on the Ocean
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why most coasts get two high tides a day and what spring and neap tides are.

levels.title: Where the Moon Came From
levels.objective: After this level you can describe the giant-impact explanation for the Moon’s origin and the evidence for it.

levels.title: Craters and Seas on the Moon
levels.objective: After this level you can explain where lunar craters and the dark “seas” came from and why they last so long.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Reading the Sky
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the everyday motions of the Sun, Moon, stars and planets and the tides they cause.

levels.title: The First Sky-Watchers
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how ancient cultures used the sky to keep calendars and navigate.

levels.title: Eratosthenes Measures the Earth
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how a shadow and a well let someone estimate Earth’s size over 2,000 years ago.

levels.title: An Earth-Centered Universe
levels.objective: After this level you can describe the geocentric model and why it lasted for more than a thousand years.

levels.title: Copernicus Moves the Sun
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the heliocentric model and why it explained retrograde motion more simply.

levels.title: Galileo’s Telescope
levels.objective: After this level you can describe what Galileo saw that challenged the Earth-centered view.

levels.title: Kepler’s Ellipses
levels.objective: After this level you can state Kepler’s laws in plain words and explain why planets speed up near the Sun.

levels.title: Newton’s Gravity
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how one law of gravity covers falling apples, orbiting moons and planets.

levels.title: Measuring the Solar System
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the astronomical unit and how astronomers measured the size of the solar system.

levels.title: New Planets: Uranus and Neptune
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how Uranus was found by telescope and Neptune was predicted by mathematics.

levels.title: Checkpoint: How We Know
levels.objective: After this level you can trace how observation and reasoning moved humanity from an Earth-centered sky to modern astronomy.

levels.title: More Than Meets the Eye: The Spectrum
levels.objective: After this level you can explain that visible light is one small part of the electromagnetic spectrum.

levels.title: Starlight’s Fingerprints
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how spectra reveal what stars are made of.

levels.title: How Telescopes Work
levels.objective: After this level you can tell refracting from reflecting telescopes and explain why bigger mirrors see more.

levels.title: Why Put Telescopes in Space?
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what Earth’s atmosphere does to starlight and what Hubble gained by leaving it.

levels.title: Listening to the Sky: Radio Astronomy
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what radio telescopes detect and why they are so large.

levels.title: Seeing Heat: Infrared and Webb
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why infrared light reveals hidden and very distant objects.

levels.title: Getting to Orbit
levels.objective: After this level you can explain that an orbit is falling around a planet, and what escape velocity means.

levels.title: Robot Explorers
levels.objective: After this level you can describe how robotic probes like Voyager explored the outer planets.

levels.title: Humans on the Moon
levels.objective: After this level you can describe the Apollo Moon landings and what they brought back.

levels.title: Checkpoint: The Tools of Astronomy
levels.objective: After this level you can match each kind of light and instrument to what it lets astronomers study.

levels.title: Mercury: The Scorched Survivor
levels.objective: After this level you can describe Mercury’s extreme temperatures and its lack of atmosphere.

levels.title: Venus: Earth’s Evil Twin
levels.objective: After this level you can compare Venus and Earth and describe Venus’s surface and odd rotation.

levels.title: Earth: The Planet We Know Best
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how Earth’s magnetic field and atmosphere protect life.

levels.title: Mars: A Planet That Lost Its Water
levels.objective: After this level you can describe the evidence that Mars once had liquid water.

levels.title: The Asteroid Belt
levels.objective: After this level you can describe the asteroid belt and why it never formed a planet.

levels.title: Jupiter’s Storms and Moons
levels.objective: After this level you can describe the Great Red Spot and Jupiter’s four large moons.

levels.title: Ocean Worlds: Europa and Enceladus
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why icy moons may hide liquid-water oceans.

levels.title: Titan: A World of Methane Lakes
levels.objective: After this level you can describe Titan’s thick atmosphere and liquid methane lakes.

levels.title: The Tilted and the Windy: Uranus and Neptune
levels.objective: After this level you can describe Uranus’s sideways tilt and Neptune’s supersonic winds.

levels.title: Milestone: The Solar System
levels.objective: After this level you can connect the planets, moons and small bodies into one picture of our solar system.

levels.title: Pluto and the Dwarf Planets
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what a dwarf planet is and why Pluto was reclassified.

levels.title: The Kuiper Belt
levels.objective: After this level you can describe the icy region beyond Neptune and what New Horizons found there.

levels.title: Comets: Dirty Snowballs
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what comets are made of and why their tails point away from the Sun.

levels.title: Shooting Stars and Meteorites
levels.objective: After this level you can tell meteoroids, meteors and meteorites apart and explain meteor showers.

levels.title: The Oort Cloud
levels.objective: After this level you can describe the distant shell of icy bodies thought to surround the solar system.

levels.title: Inside the Sun
levels.objective: After this level you can name the Sun’s layers and describe how energy travels from its core to its surface.

levels.title: Sunspots and the Solar Cycle
levels.objective: After this level you can explain sunspots and the Sun’s roughly 11-year activity cycle.

levels.title: Solar Storms and Auroras
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how solar wind and eruptions cause auroras and space weather.

levels.title: How the Solar System Formed
levels.objective: After this level you can outline how the Sun and planets formed from a collapsing cloud of gas and dust.

levels.title: Checkpoint: The Sun’s Domain
levels.objective: After this level you can describe the Sun and everything it influences, from its core to the Oort Cloud.

levels.title: Parallax: Measuring the Stars
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how parallax measures the distance to nearby stars.

levels.title: Bright or Close? Luminosity
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the difference between how bright a star looks and how bright it really is.

levels.title: The H–R Diagram
levels.objective: After this level you can read the basic pattern of the Hertzsprung–Russell diagram.

levels.title: The Main Sequence
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why a star’s mass decides its temperature and lifetime.

levels.title: Star Partners: Binary Stars
levels.objective: After this level you can explain binary stars and how they let astronomers weigh stars.

levels.title: Stellar Nurseries
levels.objective: After this level you can describe how stars form inside nebulae.

levels.title: Red Giants and Planetary Nebulae
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how Sun-like stars swell and shed their outer layers.

levels.title: White Dwarfs
levels.objective: After this level you can describe white dwarfs and why they slowly cool.

levels.title: Supernovae and Star Stuff
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how massive stars explode and scatter the elements we are made of.

levels.title: Checkpoint: The Lives of Stars
levels.objective: After this level you can trace a star’s life from nebula to its final state based on its mass.

levels.title: Neutron Stars
levels.objective: After this level you can describe neutron stars and how dense they are.

levels.title: Pulsars: Cosmic Lighthouses
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what pulsars are and how they were discovered.

levels.title: Black Holes
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what a black hole is and how one forms.

levels.title: The Event Horizon
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the event horizon and what the first black hole image showed.

levels.title: The Black Hole at Our Center
levels.objective: After this level you can describe Sagittarius A* and how astronomers found it.

levels.title: Gravitational Waves
levels.objective: After this level you can explain gravitational waves and how LIGO first detected them.

levels.title: Finding Exoplanets
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the transit and wobble methods for finding planets around other stars.

levels.title: The Habitable Zone
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the habitable zone and why liquid water matters.

levels.title: The Search for Life
levels.objective: After this level you can describe how scientists look for signs of life beyond Earth.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Extreme Objects and Other Worlds
levels.objective: After this level you can compare the remnants stars leave behind and explain how we find other worlds.

levels.title: Kinds of Galaxies
levels.objective: After this level you can tell spiral, elliptical and irregular galaxies apart.

levels.title: Inside the Milky Way
levels.objective: After this level you can describe the Milky Way’s disk, spiral arms, central bulge and halo.

levels.title: When Galaxies Collide
levels.objective: After this level you can explain galaxy collisions and the future merger of the Milky Way and Andromeda.

levels.title: The Local Group
levels.objective: After this level you can describe the small group of galaxies the Milky Way belongs to.

levels.title: Dark Matter
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the evidence for dark matter from how galaxies spin.

levels.title: Galaxy Clusters and Gravitational Lenses
levels.objective: After this level you can describe galaxy clusters and how their gravity bends light.

levels.title: Quasars and Active Galaxies
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how feeding supermassive black holes can outshine whole galaxies.

levels.title: Hubble’s Expanding Universe
levels.objective: After this level you can explain Hubble’s discovery that galaxies are moving apart.

levels.title: Redshift
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how redshift reveals that the universe is expanding.

levels.title: Checkpoint: A Universe of Galaxies
levels.objective: After this level you can describe the structure of the universe from single galaxies to clusters.

levels.title: The Big Bang
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what the Big Bang theory says and what it doesn’t.

levels.title: The Afterglow: Cosmic Microwave Background
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the cosmic microwave background and why it supports the Big Bang.

levels.title: The First Stars and Galaxies
levels.objective: After this level you can describe how the first stars and galaxies lit up the early universe.

levels.title: Dark Energy
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the discovery that the universe’s expansion is speeding up.

levels.title: How Big Is the Observable Universe?
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why the observable universe is larger than 13.8 billion light-years across.

levels.title: Integration: From Atoms to Galaxies
levels.objective: After this level you can connect nuclear fusion, stellar lives and galaxy formation into one story.

levels.title: Integration: How We Know What We Know
levels.objective: After this level you can connect each major astronomical discovery to the tool or method behind it.

levels.title: Integration: Futures of the Sun, Earth and Universe
levels.objective: After this level you can describe the long-term futures of the Sun, Earth, Milky Way and universe.

levels.title: Integration: The Big Open Questions
levels.objective: After this level you can describe the major unanswered questions in astronomy and why they matter.

levels.title: Mastery Challenge: Astronomy
levels.objective: After this level you can demonstrate command of Astronomy Levels 1–99 across the whole tree.
